task: J0365: timed Shorts plate boards v01 from locked vo_v02 takes. 100% reuse of the long's KEEP plate boards (0 extra Flow credits). Mint nothing.

shorts.youtube_title: Why Doesn't the Moon Fall to Earth?
shorts.promoted_long_title: Why Doesn't the Moon Fall to Earth?
shorts.frame0_change_by_1s: Moon already gliding along its curved path above Earth's limb at frame 0; dotted tangent and drop arrows ink in by 1.0 s.

teach_overlay.band: 16:9 centre band (clear of 0–2 s hook and 9–14 s title)

rows.spoken: The Moon is falling towards the Earth right now.
rows.crop_9x16: 9:16 crop on the Moon curving above Earth's horizon; hook caption ALWAYS FALLING at 0.0–2.0 s.

rows.spoken: Every second, it moves sideways about a kilometre, and drops a tiny bit towards us.
rows.crop_9x16: 9:16 crop on KEEP £0 parchment code graphic P3:08_km_a_second; DATA label 'ABOUT 1 KM A SECOND' at 3.0–6.8 s.

rows.spoken: But the Earth curves away beneath it, so it keeps on missing.
rows.crop_9x16: 9:16 crop on Newton's mountain cannonball curving all the way around Earth; promoted long title card on screen 9.0–14.0 s.

rows.spoken: Isaac Newton worked this out, more than three hundred years ago.
rows.crop_9x16: 9:16 crop on young Isaac Newton in the Woolsthorpe orchard looking up at the daytime Moon.

rows.spoken: An orbit isn't floating at all. It's falling, and missing, for ever.
rows.crop_9x16: Final 4 s (20.32–24.32 s) returns to P1:01_moon_falling so the Short loops seamlessly into frame 0.

shorts.promoted_long_title: Why Doesn't the Moon Fall to Earth?
shorts.frame0_change_by_1s: Apple and Moon split comparison already dropping at frame 0; both reach the same mark by 1.0 s.

teach_overlay.band: 16:9 centre band (clear of 0–2 s hook and 9–14 s title)

rows.spoken: In one minute, the Moon falls about as far as an apple falls in one second.
rows.crop_9x16: 9:16 crop on split comparison of apple drop (1 s) vs Moon drop (1 min); hook caption 1 MINUTE = 1 SECOND at 0.0–2.0 s.
9:16 crop on Newton at his desk comparing the two columns.

rows.spoken: The Moon is sixty times further from the Earth's centre than we are,
rows.crop_9x16: 9:16 crop on KEEP £0 parchment code graphic P4:03_sixty_earths (60 Earth radii); promoted long title on screen 9.0–14.0 s.

rows.spoken: so the pull on it is sixty times sixty weaker. Three thousand six hundred times.
rows.crop_9x16: 9:16 crop on KEEP £0 parchment code graphic P4:04_dots_square (60×60 grid); DATA overlay '3,600 TIMES WEAKER' at 14.5–18.2 s.

rows.spoken: And the numbers matched. One pull, for apples and Moons.
rows.crop_9x16: Final 4.14 s returns to P4:05_minute_second so the Short loops seamlessly into frame 0.
